courseTitle: 100 Days of Code: JavaScript Data Structures and Algorithms

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to learn about hash terminology.
Now you might be interested why we are learning about the terminology.
Now this is very crucial for especially interviews.
When they are asking the interview questions they are going to use the hashing terminologies that you
need to understand.
So let's look at them one by one.
So we have said that we have a magic function which is called hash function.
And it's going to take input and convert this input to a number which is going to be the index in this
table over here.
So we are going to place the key and value pair to this index based on this function.
So this function is called hash function.
By definition it's a function that can be used to map the data of arbitrary size to the data of fixed
size.
So before we have said that this is a magic function which converts the strings to the some numbers
to store them in arrays based on the cell index.
So in terms of hash tables this is called hash function.
Now the next terminology is the key.
So the key is the input data given by the user.
Now here again as we did before we are passing key as a parameter.
And we are getting a number which is going to be the index of cell and saving it into this array.
So you just need to know that any value that we are passing to this function is called key.
Now the next terminology is hash value.
Now the value that we are getting from out of this function is going to call hash value.
So we are passing key.
And this key is converted to hash value based on the hash function.
Now the next terminology is hash table.
So it's a data structure.
In this case it is an array where we are saving the key and value pairs based on the value that we are
getting from the hash table.
So all information will be saved inside the hash table.
Now the last terminology over here is collision.
Now what is collision.
So let's say we have already inserted Apple and ten key value pairs at the index of three.
Now, if I want to insert the second key and value pairs, which is Mongo and 15, in this case we are
going to take the key which is Mongo, and pass it to this hash function.
And it's going to give us the number where we can save this key and value pairs.
Now in this case the question is what if it gives us the same number that is already filled.
So in this case it's going to try to insert to this field and it's going to cause the collision.
So whenever you hear the term collision it means that when two different keys has the same hash value.
In this case it's going to cause the collision.
Of course there are resolution techniques for handling the collision.
We are going to learn them in our upcoming lectures here.
You just need to know that if two keys have the same hash value, in this case, it's going to cause
collision.
Now this is all for hash terminologies.
Now in the next lecture we are going to look at the some sample hash functions.
